page: Amazon Web Services c9g.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and powered by custom AWS Graviton processors based on the 64-bit ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 architecture. The instance offers 8 dedicated physical CPU cores running at a fixed clock speed of 3.3 GHz without hyperthreading. Memory provisioned for this server type is 16.0 GB, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio with 2.0 GB of memory per core. Cache configuration includes 64 KB L1d, 2 MB L2, and 48 MB L3 cache. It contains no attached local NVMe storage and zero discrete GPUs. Network performance is rated at a 4 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Benchmark evaluation demonstrates strong single-thread performance and memory bandwidth efficiency on the Arm64 architecture. The server achieved top-tier relative results in Geekbench single-core execution (score of 2361.0), Geekbench text processing (3155.0), bzip3 single-threaded decompression (17.08 GB/sec), and PassMark memory operations (3725.39). Single-threaded gzip compression rated in the top 25% at 36.29 GB/sec, while small-model LLM text generation achieved strong performance at 298.71 tokens/sec. Conversely, PassMark CPU encryption performance scored lower relative to competing instances due to missing specialized hardware instructions like VAES, and prompt processing for medium-sized LLM models measured lower at 22.5 tokens/sec.

The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and high single-core efficiency make this instance suitable for compute-heavy, single-thread bound, or CPU-dense workloads such as web application compilation, text parsing, lightweight LLM token generation, and CPU-driven microservices. Workloads requiring local ephemeral storage require attached Elastic Block Store volumes, while memory-intensive databases or heavy vector cryptography routines may encounter architectural tradeoffs under sustained heavy load.
description: Amazon Web Services c9g.2xlarge is a compute-optimized Arm64 instance featuring 8 dedicated ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 physical cores clocked at 3.3 GHz and 16.0 GB of system memory. Operating on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the server delivers a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, 48 MB L3 cache, and 4 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, with zero local ephemeral storage or GPUs attached. Benchmark evaluations highlight top-tier performance in single-threaded tasks, including Geekbench single-core testing, text processing, bzip3 decompression, and system memory bandwidth. Single-threaded gzip compression and lightweight model LLM text generation also demonstrate strong relative throughput. Weaknesses appear in specialized encryption instruction execution and medium-model prompt processing. The instance provides cost-effective dedicated CPU compute power for compilation tasks, text processing, microservices, and general compute-heavy workloads that do not require attached local SSD storage.
